skill.name: nansen-general-search
skill.description: Search Nansen for crypto tokens or labeled entities by name, then return matching addresses and metadata.
skill.summary: Find token addresses and Nansen entity matches from a name search.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick findings are false positives; they are code fences and inline flag formatting. The NANSEN_API_KEY findings are confirmed because the skill requires a secret-bearing environment variable for the Nansen CLI, with no evidence of prompt injection or data exfiltration in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: API key exposure through CLI environment
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated Nansen API key with minimal scope, avoid printing environment variables, and document how the CLI consumes the key.
Pin or verify the nansen-cli package version before installation and keep the allowed Bash pattern limited to nansen commands.

content.value_statement: Blockchain researchers often need a token address or entity match from a plain name. This skill runs Nansen search commands and returns concise matches with useful fields.
actual_capabilities: Search Nansen for tokens by case-insensitive name text.
Search Nansen for entities by name with a result limit.
Filter token searches by blockchain using the chain option.
Request selected result fields such as address, name, symbol, and chain.
Explain when address lookup should use profiler labels instead of search.
limitations: Requires the nansen CLI and a valid NANSEN_API_KEY.
Does not match directly by address.
Depends on Nansen data availability and API permissions.
Search results are limited by the CLI maximum result count.

use_cases.title: Resolve Token Addresses
use_cases.description: Find likely token matches by name before checking address, symbol, and chain details.

use_cases.title: Identify Known Entities
use_cases.description: Search for entity names and review a small set of possible Nansen matches.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Inputs
use_cases.description: Collect normalized names, addresses, and chains for downstream wallet or token analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Token
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nansen search to find token matches for "jupiter". Show address, name, symbol, and chain when available.

prompt_templates.title: Search an Entity
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Nansen for the entity name "Vitalik" and limit results to five. Summarize each likely match.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Find token matches for "bonk" on Solana only. Return the most relevant fields and explain any ambiguity.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Nansen for these names: "jupiter", "bonk", and "aave". Separate token and entity results, include chains, and note unresolved names.

output_examples.output: Jupiter token candidates are listed with matching names, symbols, chains, and contract addresses. Ambiguous matches are grouped for follow-up verification.

output_examples.input: Search for Vitalik as an entity.
output_examples.output: A short entity list is returned with names and available labels. Results are limited to the requested count.

output_examples.input: Find bonk on Solana and show only key fields.
output_examples.output: Solana results are filtered to likely Bonk matches. Each result includes the requested identifying fields when Nansen provides them.

best_practices: Use the smallest result limit that answers the research question.
Verify token addresses before using them in transactions or reports.
Use a dedicated Nansen API key and rotate it when access changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as proof that a token is safe or endorsed.
Do not search by address; use the appropriate address lookup workflow.
Do not expose API keys in prompts, logs, screenshots, or shared outputs.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches Nansen for token names and entity names, then returns matching records from the CLI.

faq.question: Can it search by wallet or contract address?
faq.answer: No. The source instructions state that address lookup should use profiler labels instead.

faq.question: Does it require a Nansen account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the nansen CLI and a valid NANSEN_API_KEY with suitable access.

faq.question: Can I limit the number of results?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports a result limit, with the CLI maximum noted as 50.

faq.question: Can it filter results by chain?
faq.answer: Yes. Token searches can be filtered by chain when the CLI supports that filter.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
